# Deck slide map and short scripts (auto-generated by v2_reflective/build_deck_clean.py on every build; do not edit)

Same text as the PowerPoint / Google Slides speaker notes. Longer scripts: `Presenter_Notes.md`, Part 0.

| Slide | Title | Short script (speaker note) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agentic Self-Correction in LLaMA-3 | Title. Say: we take one LLM review-rating method from a published paper, rebuild it, find where it falls short, and replace it with several agents that rate, explain and check. |
| 2 | One model, one pass, nothing checks it | Problem. Today a single LLM reads a review and gives a star and a justification. Three things go wrong: no second opinion, the explanation cannot be checked, and hard language (mixed or negative-sounding but positive reviews) trips it up. Keep it to one minute. |
| 3 | Phase 1 · The reference paper | Section 1. Say: we chose Wang et al. (2025) as our reference paper. Phase 1 is our reproduction of it and our exploration of it. |
| 4 | One fine-tuned LLaMA rates each review | The paper we chose. Walk the pipeline left to right: clean the data with TextBlob, balance the stars, fine-tune LLaMA-3-8B with a small LoRA add-on, then one prompt gives a star and a justification. The paper reports 92.6% on its own data and protocol. Source: Wang et al. (2025), ITM Web of Conferences 70, 04021. |
| 5 | Three problems when we rebuilt it | Exploration findings. (1) Leak audit (LOG 2026-10-11): choosing the one-shot example from the true star inflates accuracy; with a random example it drops 7.7 points (59.7 to 52.0). Be fair: the leak was in our first reproduction's example choice, not a claim about the authors. (2) Preprocessing ablation: TextBlob cleaning removes most negative reviews, 52% of 1-star and 67% of 2-star. (3) Explanation study (x1_explain_compare.out): Phase 1 produced only 5 distinct sentences for 150 reviews and never quoted the review. |
| 6 | Right direction, wrong star | Phase 1 results (results_frozen.md). The reference method retrained on Electronics, leak-free: exact star 54.0% balanced, 53.4% natural, but within one star 93.7% / 94.4%. It gets the direction right and the exact star wrong. The 92.6% used a different protocol and is not comparable. Data: frozen disjoint splits; every choice on dev; test sets read once. |
| 7 | Phase 2 · Several agents | Section 2. Say the principle out loud: three attempts to let an LLM decide the star failed, so trained models decide, the LLM explains, and checks keep the explanation honest. |
| 8 | How a review is rated and explained | Phase 2 system. Left: three independent agents read the review. The LLaMA probe is a classifier on a frozen LLaMA-3-8B layer (meaning). The Evidence model is TF-IDF + logistic regression (key words). DeBERTa-v3 is a fine-tuned encoder (wording). The Reflector, a logistic regression on their probabilities, decides the star. Right: the Hand-off agent answers only when confident; the Explainer writes from the evidence and the Critic checks it and sends it back, up to four rewrites. Built in LangGraph. The Router (skip the probe when sure) failed its check with three agents and is off. |
| 9 | Results | Section 3. Say: every number from here on comes from test sets that were read once, after all choices were made on development data. |
| 10 | Phase 2 gets the exact star far more often | Headline (results_frozen.md, analysis_C.out). Exact star: Phase 1 54.0 / 53.4, Phase 2 67.5 / 78.0, that is +13.5 and +24.6 points, 29% and 53% fewer errors, significant after Holm correction over 12 comparisons. Within one star 97.3 / 97.4. If asked whether 67.5 is good: random is 20%, exact five-star rating is hard because neighbouring stars are ambiguous. Caveat if asked: on balanced eval the three-agent stack ties the previous two-agent stack; DeBERTa's +2.3 is on the natural mix. |
| 11 | Each agent is strong where another is weak | Why several agents beat one (agents_complement.png, q5_breakdown / complement outputs). Left: the Evidence model wins on short reviews, the LLaMA probe on long reviews, and the combined stack is best or near-best in every length band. Right: when the probe and the Evidence model disagree, the stack still gets 58-62% right, against 36-50% for either alone. |
| 12 | Reviews that sound negative but are rated 4–5★ | Hard cases (hard_cases.out). Reviews whose words sound negative but whose star is 4 or 5. Phase 1 gets 35.0% (eval, n 40) and 43.0% (natural, n 193); Phase 2 gets 67.5% and 78.2%. p 0.0023 and 5.4e-16. If asked: positive-sounding 1-2 star reviews improve by about 10 points but not significantly; explicit sarcasm is too rare to measure (6 and 1 reviews). |
| 13 | When it is wrong, it is almost always one star off | Errors (cm_main_eval.png, results_frozen.md). Confusion matrix on balanced eval: mistakes hug the diagonal. Within one star 97.3% balanced, 97.4% natural; 92% (balanced) and 88% (natural) of errors are one star off. Mean absolute error 0.35 / 0.25 stars. |
| 14 | Answer when sure, ask a person when not | Hand-off agent (s1_selective.out). The threshold is fixed on dev2 before the tests. On the natural test it answers 56% of reviews automatically and is right 92.8% of the time; on balanced eval 86.9% on 41%. What it hands to a person is only 54-59% right, so those really are the hard ones. Phase 1 with the same rule reaches 66.9% on balanced eval. Star ranges (q1_conformal.out): instead of handing off, it can give a range that holds the true star 90% of the time, 1.44 stars wide on natural (Phase 1 2.08). |
| 15 | The Critic makes explanations faithful | Critic loop (b2_report.out). The Explainer writes from the evidence only; the Critic checks five things: the star matches, every quote is really in the review, it uses the key phrases, it mentions disagreement, and an LLM judge finds no invented claim. Faithful first drafts 62.3% / 63.7%; after up to four rewrites 90.5% / 91.6%. 841 fixed, 0 broken. Deletion test: removing the cited phrases lowers the model's confidence about twice as much as removing random words (0.156 vs 0.077 eval). |
| 16 | One review, three drafts | Worked example from the live demo (presentation/demo_cache.json, balanced eval). Read the review, then the drafts left to right: the Critic names exactly what is wrong (an invented phrase, too few key phrases), and draft 3 passes all five checks. Compare: Phase 1's justification never quotes the review. |
| 17 | A person checked the Critic | Human check (human_check.out, LOG 2026-11-20). The author marked 50 random explanations, blind to the Critic. Overall the author found 80% faithful, the Critic 92%, agreement 76%. Split: when all agents agreed (34) the author passed every one; when they disagreed (16) only 37.5%, while the Critic passed 93.8%. In those the Explainer says things about the system ("the reviewer gave N stars", a confidence %) that no check catches. Say it plainly: the Critic is too lenient on contested reviews; one annotator and 50 items, so an indication. |
| 18 | Stable under messy text, but needs the title | Robustness (q4_robustness.out, 300 eval reviews). Share of reviews whose star changes when the text is changed. Typos: Phase 2 0.7% vs Phase 1 2.0% (ns). Flat text (no punctuation or capitals): 9.3% vs 29.7%. No title: 15.7% vs 0%, because the Evidence model and DeBERTa read the title and Phase 1 does not. Say the limitation plainly. |
| 19 | Negative results we report | Failures (EXPERIMENTS_SUMMARY.md). Every idea had a pass/fail rule written before it ran and was checked on development data only; none touched the test sets. Three attempts to let an LLM decide or revise the star failed (the last: 76 fixed vs 89 broken). A second LLM judge (Qwen2.5-7B) rejected every explanation. The Router saved work with two agents but failed its check with three, so it is off. |
| 20 | What the project shows | Conclusions. Three points: (1) the reference method, rebuilt leak-free, gets 54% exact; we found a label leak, a cleaning step that removes negative reviews, and template justifications. (2) Three agents and a Reflector reach 67.5% / 78.0%, +13.5 / +24.6 points, significant. (3) The agentic layer makes the output checkable: 91-92% faithful explanations, 0 broken; Hand-off 93% right on 56%; and a human check shows where the Critic is still too lenient. Limits: one dataset, needs the title. |
| 21 | Thank you | Close. Offer the live demo notebook (presentation/Final_Demo.ipynb): five reviews rated, explained and checked, Phase 1 next to Phase 2. |
